pr.title: Set the panel's review requests apart from your pull requests with a blank line
pr.head: 7715feb9ebf67d2d9b7975ecfbeca4840371192b

summary: Projector's panel is the list that its Claude Code mod draws above the prompt. It shows the pull requests your session fixes or reviews, one line each, and under them the inbox: questions, requests, and notices that agents posted for you. The pull requests come in two sections. Your own pull requests come first, then the review requests, which is what the panel calls pull requests that someone else wrote.

Before this change, the two sections ran together, and the only sign of where yours ended was the author column starting on the first review request. This change draws a blank line between the two sections, the same way a blank line already sets the inbox items apart from the pull requests. The line appears only when both sections show something, either their rows or, when you collapse a section from the header, its one + line. With no pull requests of your own, or no review requests, the list starts and ends as before.

The review of this head asks for one change: docs/plugins.md still draws its example panel with no blank line between a pull request of yours and a review request, and its prose does not mention the line.

groups.title: A blank line between your pull requests and the review requests
groups.kicker: How the panel's render places the new line, and the tests that pin it
intro: The panel's render builds the pull request part of the list from PR_SECTIONS, the two sections pr (yours) and review (everyone else's), in that order. For each section it takes the section's collapsed line from expander, which is empty unless the section is collapsed, and then the section's rows from drawRow, unless the section is collapsed.

The change collects each section's lines into prLines and drops a section that has none. It then joins what remains with a <Text key="before-reviews"> </Text> before every section but the first. Because there are only two sections, that is at most one blank line, and only when both have something to show.

checks.text: A collapsed section with no rows never earns the blank line. isCollapsed is true only while the header has a count for the section, and an empty section has none, so its expander output and its rows are both empty and prLines drops it. Checked by reading isCollapsed and expander at this head.

The hooks module's tests pass at this head: claude plugin test . reported 237 pass and 0 fail, and hooks/typecheck.sh and both claude plugin validate runs passed, through project review gate. CI's check job passed too.

files.note: The panel's render: the pull request sections are now collected into prLines, empty ones dropped, and joined with one blank line.

checks.text: A drawer opened under a collapsed section's line, or under the last of your rows, belongs to that section's lines, so it stays above the blank line rather than below it.

The living documentation is out of date. docs/plugins.md's first example panel, at lines 280 to 282, still puts the review request #258 directly under your #267, and the paragraph at lines 354 to 356 does not mention the blank line. The repository's CLAUDE.md asks for docs/ to change in the same pull request as the behavior it describes. An open pull request that stops counting threads on a row rewrites that same example block, so whichever merges second resolves it.

files.note: Three existing panel tests gain assertions about the blank line: exactly one, between the sections, with rows; one between the two collapsed lines; and none once only review requests are left.

checks.text: The first test used to assert that the list had no blank line at all. It now asserts exactly one, and that the review request author bob appears only after it.
With both sections collapsed, the text right after your last label, y#7, must be the blank line and then the review requests' +. Without the separator it would be + directly.
This assertion catches the line opening the list when your own section is empty, as it would if empty sections were not dropped from prLines.
